final_anchors.quote: The unindexed Record-content distribution is a different object: `p(E)=sum_{j:E_j=E}q_j`. Its support consists of contents with positive summed mass. Equal matrices do not encode the index `j`; implementing or registering that extra label is an open physical bridge. If a supplied state gives some `q_j=0`, that index is not in probability support even though its effect remains in the algebraic tuple. A strictly positive-support reading would need its own positivity restriction.

resolved_original_findings.original_title: State raw and conditional sign probabilities separately
resolved_original_findings.author_disposition: Raw rank-one refinements retain p; mixed tuple has cp,c(1-p),1-c, with directional conditional p. A sign is sampled, not erased or forced. Actual1/4,1/4,1/2 counterexample and original35state/scale tests retained.

final_anchors.quote: > **Sign identities.** Write `p=tr(rho P(m))`. In a rank-one collinear refinement the positive-direction entries sum to `P(m)`, so their **raw** total probability is `p`. In the mixed tuple `(cP(m),cP(-m),(1-c)I)` the raw probabilities are `(cp,c(1-p),1-c)`; only conditional on a directional outcome are the sign odds `(p,1-p)`. The scalar-identity outcome has no direction under R1. S3 retains the original five-state/seven-scale arithmetic with this corrected interpretation, and Q4 checks the actual mixed counterexample.

resolved_original_findings.original_title: Expose the joint-resampling assumption and preserve Record permanence
resolved_original_findings.author_disposition: Product powers are only supplied independent one-shot auxiliary readout arithmetic, with no overwriting of permanent Records. Even-parity8bit example defeats product inference from all local six-conditioned fair marginals; fixed flip patterns do not imply stochastic survival.

final_anchors.quote: For a **supplied auxiliary independent one-shot readout of `N^2` fresh outcomes**, all-plus probability is `2^(-N^2)` at `p=1/2`, giving `10^-173.4,10^-308.3,10^-693.6` for `N=24,32,48`. At `p=5/6` it is `(5/6)^(N^2)`, giving `10^-45.6,10^-81.1,10^-182.4`. These are conditional product arithmetic, not an axiom-native joint law and not an operation overwriting permanent Records. Even every single-bit conditional on any six other bits being fair does not imply a product: the uniform even-parity law on eight bits satisfies all such conditionals but assigns all-zero probability `1/128`, versus `1/256` independently. Q5 checks all 3,584 such conditioned cases.
PARITY_STATES = [bits for bits in product((0, 1), repeat=8) if sum(bits) % 2 == 0]

resolved_original_findings.original_title: Certify the whole spectral window or label the count as sampled
resolved_original_findings.author_disposition: Complete1152eigenpair basis replaces nearest60; unchanged matrices/window/core threshold/patterns. Four actual windows16/34/68/48, core2/2/0/2, residual/orthogonality controls. Numerical individual-vector degeneracy dependence explicit.

final_anchors.quote: The float64 model uses the original relaxed `24x24` open-plane field (`M_0=0.7`, 960 free sites, residual about `9.9e-15`) and four original deterministic sign patterns. The corrected solver diagonalizes **all 1,152 states** of each matrix at `q=pi+0.1`, checks residuals/orthogonality, and reports every state with `|E|<0.686`. Core means an individual normalized computed vector has weight greater than `0.6` on `hypot(x-c_x,y-c_y)<5`. This criterion is basis-sensitive in degenerate eigenspaces. The original nearest-60 calculation missed eight of the 68 window states for the named `1/2` pattern; the complete calculation still finds zero core vectors there, and two for each other declared pattern. This is a finite deterministic comparison, not a random-sign survival theorem, a general density threshold, or a thermodynamic statement.
